theme: FRED / BEA / BLS / Census API clients and curated macro panels (consumer sentiment, PCE services, CPI lodging, airfares, unemployment by metro)
queries_run: gh search repos "bea api" python --limit 30 --sort stars
gh search repos "bls api" python --limit 30 --sort stars
gh search repos "census api" python client --limit 30 --sort stars
gh search repos "consumer sentiment" "unemployment" metro --limit 30 --sort stars
WebFetch raw README mortada/fredapi (ALFRED vintage check)

candidates.name: mortada/fredapi
candidates.what_it_holds: Python client (1657 stars, Apache-2.0, updated 13 Sep 2026) wrapping BOTH FRED and ALFRED. Confirmed via README: get_series_first_release(), get_series_as_of_date(), get_series_all_releases(), get_series_vintage_dates() — full point-in-time/vintage retrieval for any FRED series (CPI lodging away from home, CPI airline fares, Univ. Michigan consumer sentiment (UMCSENT), PCE services, metro-level unemployment via LAUS series, etc.). No data files committed; it is a live-pull method against the free FRED API (no key cost beyond a free registration).
candidates.why_useful: Directly answers gap #4 (point-in-time / vintage macro series, ALFRED-style). CONTEXT.md says the team already holds ~40 FRED series but does not say they are vintage-aware; this library lets every FRED input in the model (CPI lodging, airfares, sentiment) be refit at each historical guide date instead of using today's revised values, which is exactly the point-in-time rule (Rule 2) the repo's own CLAUDE.md enforces for consensus data and should extend to macro inputs too.
candidates.time_coverage: varies by series, many back to 1940s-1990s; ALFRED vintages from first FRED digitization (~1990s onward for most series)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Team already holds ~40 FRED series (non-vintage per CONTEXT.md); this specific library adds ALFRED vintage capability which is not confirmed as already in use

candidates.name: us-bea/beaapi
candidates.what_it_holds: Official BEA-maintained Python package (69 stars, CC0-1.0, updated 10 Sep 2026) for pulling BEA API tables (NIPA, including PCE by category — e.g. PCE: Foreign travel, PCE: Air transportation, PCE: Accommodations — and regional/state personal income). No data committed; live pull, requires free BEA API key (not paid).
candidates.why_useful: Official client for the BEA PCE travel/accommodation subcomponents CONTEXT.md already lists holding a 'BEA PCE travel panel' — this is likely the underlying tool or an equivalent, useful to confirm/replace an ad hoc BEA pull and to get PCE line items at finer granularity (e.g. state personal income by quarter) than a generic panel.
candidates.time_coverage: BEA NIPA history, generally 1929-present annual, 1947-present quarterly for national accounts
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Overlaps with existing BEA PCE travel panel; flagged because it is the maintainer-official client and adds state/regional PCE granularity not confirmed in current holding

candidates.name: nagaatwork/laborlens
candidates.what_it_holds: BLS API -> Snowflake -> dbt -> Streamlit pipeline for US labor market data, all 50 states + DC, unemployment rate, SARIMA 6-month-ahead forecasts, monthly refresh via GitHub Actions. Confirmed via README: state-level only (not metro despite description ambiguity), no data files committed to repo (pulled live via BLS API + requires a Snowflake account to run).
candidates.why_useful: A working reference pipeline for BLS unemployment-by-state if the team wants a state-level (not metro) unemployment panel as a regional consumer-strength proxy for the NA segment split; but it is state-level, requires Snowflake, and holds no committed data, so it's a method template rather than a data source.
candidates.geography: US, all 50 states + DC (state-level, not metro)
candidates.size_hint: n/a (no committed data; needs external Snowflake account to run)

candidates.name: siddarth-bantula/us-labor-market-analytics
candidates.what_it_holds: End-to-end labor market analytics pipeline using BLS API, Python ETL, Power BI (0 stars, updated 28 Aug 2026, no license). Similar shape to laborlens: BLS API extraction + ETL + BI dashboard, not confirmed to commit raw data files.
candidates.why_useful: Second BLS-API ETL template; lower quality signal (0 stars, no README depth checked) than laborlens/fredapi. Included for completeness in case its ETL scripts target metro-level LAUS series the team could reuse.

candidates.name: lachlandeer/bls-api-to-csv
candidates.what_it_holds: Small Python script (2 stars) that queries the BLS API for a given series ID and writes results to CSV — a minimal, easily-adapted reference implementation, not a curated panel or committed dataset.
candidates.why_useful: Simplest possible template for a point-in-time-aware BLS pull (CPI lodging away from home series CUUR0000SEHB, CPI airline fares CUUR0000SETG01, or metro-level LAUS unemployment series) if the team wants to write its own minimal client rather than adopt a heavier framework.
candidates.geography: US (whatever BLS series ID is queried)

candidates.name: govex/bls-oews-api-tutorial
candidates.what_it_holds: Tutorial (MIT license, updated 7 Jan 2026) for querying BLS OEWS (Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics) survey data via the BLS API — a walkthrough, not a stored dataset.
candidates.why_useful: OEWS gives industry/occupation employment and wages, which is a weak but real proxy for hospitality/leisure-sector labor demand by area if the team ever wants a labor-market-based travel-industry proxy. Marginal fit to the theme's core (macro consumer/travel series), included as a low-confidence adjacent method.

candidates.name: timlenardo/py_census_api
candidates.what_it_holds: Minimal Python client (0 stars, MIT, last updated 2014) for querying the US Census Bureau Data API. Very old, unmaintained (12 years stale), unverified whether it still works against current Census API versions.
candidates.why_useful: Could in principle be adapted to pull Census ACS/Population estimates by metro (a denominator for per-capita travel/booking metrics) or Census Household Pulse Survey (a real-time consumer-behavior survey with some travel/spending questions), but staleness makes it a weak candidate — flagged mainly because gh search turned up no better Census-specific client in this pass.

candidates.name: leaderanalytics/Vyntix.Fred.FredClient
candidates.what_it_holds: .NET/C# client (7 stars, updated 18 Apr 2026) for the St. Louis Fed FRED API, part of a broader 'Vyntix' suite (see also Vyntix.Fred.Domain) that appears oriented toward storing FRED data with vintage/versioning semantics given the product name Vyntix (implies 'vintage-index').
candidates.why_useful: Non-Python alternative FRED client; the 'Vyntix' branding suggests explicit vintage-data handling similar to ALFRED, which would be directly relevant to gap #4, but this was not verified by fetching the README (budget) — flagged as worth a follow-up check rather than confirmed high value.

notes: Hard limit of 6 gh search repos calls was used exactly (fredapi, bea api python, beaapi, bls api python, census api python client, consumer-sentiment+unemployment+metro). The last query (consumer sentiment / unemployment / metro combined) returned zero results — gh search repos free-text matching is weak for multi-concept queries; better results came from single-tool-name queries (fredapi, beaapi). Did not find any GitHub repo with a COMMITTED curated macro panel specific to ABNB-relevant series (CPI lodging, airfares, consumer sentiment) bundled together as static files -- everything found is either an API client (acquisition_method) or a generic/unrelated labor-market ETL demo project. Did not find a working Census API client better than a 2014 unmaintained script; a follow-up scout could try `gh search repos topic:census-api` or `gh search repos "census bureau" ACS python` since our one Census query underperformed. Did not find any repo specifically combining FRED+BEA+BLS+Census into one 'macro panel for equity research' package -- this looks like a real gap the team could fill itself using mortada/fredapi (confirmed ALFRED support) + us-bea/beaapi as the two solid building blocks. WebSearch tool was unavailable (session budget exhausted at 200/200 before this scout could use it), so could not cross-check with generic web search beyond gh CLI + 2 WebFetch README checks; if another scout still has WebSearch budget, worth trying 'Michigan consumer sentiment API github' and 'CPI lodging series ID python github' directly.
